title: C1 — analysis configuration (the interrupt model)
description: The hand-written configuration file. It is the tool's specification of the interrupt model and it BOUNDS the analysis: cost follows code reachable from the declared entry points, not repository size (wiki/Pipeline Design.md). Owner: Track A. Consumers: Track A, Track C. Deciding to hand-write this rather than infer it is recorded in wiki/concepts/Specification Inference.md.

source_root.description: Paths in context records are made relative to this.

sources.description: Files or directories. A single file is the benchmark mode; a directory is the whole-repository mode (Pipeline Design, 'Two input modes').

mode.description: 'link' = per-TU clang -emit-llvm then llvm-link. 'intercept' = wllvm/gllvm around the project's own build. Never merge at the C source level: it destroys source ranges and collides static symbols (Pipeline Design).

flags.description: -g is mandatory: DILocation is what makes the source mapping possible. -O0 alone marks functions optnone and the pass manager skips them, hence -disable-O0-optnone.

extra_bitcode.description: Additional .bc to llvm-link in — e.g. the benchmark's common.c.

priority_convention.description: Fixed by decree and stated explicitly because the published papers disagree with the benchmarks (Contradictions #3). Present in the file so that every run manifest records it.

flows.description: Every flow is a root of its own reachability analysis. A handler missing from this list contributes no accesses and its defects become invisible — the single most recall-critical field in the file.

irq_arg.description: Zero-based index of the argument naming the interrupt. null means the primitive affects all interrupts unconditionally (e.g. a bare cli()/sti()).

all_value.description: Argument value meaning 'all interrupts'. Racebench uses -1.

non_constant_arg.description: What to assume when the argument is not a compile-time constant. 'unknown' is the recall-safe choice for 'disable' (nothing is proven masked) and is the default.

initial_state.description: Masking state at the entry of each flow. Racebench's init() calls enable_isr(-1), so all-enabled matches. 'unknown' is the safe default for unfamiliar platforms.

isr_entry_masks_self.description: Whether hardware masks an interrupt while its own handler runs. Affects re-entrancy; recorded in the manifest because it changes the candidate set.

semantics.description: The two open semantic decisions are exposed here as explicit, defaulted, labelled settings rather than buried (Dashboard Design R10; wiki/Open Questions.md).

equal_priority_preemption.description: May two flows of equal priority preempt each other? Default true = recall-safe. svp_real_002 has two ISRs sharing priority 1 and no tool in the corpus models this.

isr_arrival.description: Racebench's README states interrupts are non-periodic and may fire an unspecified number of times at unspecified points. 'unbounded' matches; anything narrower is an unsound filter.

nesting.description: May an ISR be preempted by a strictly higher-priority ISR? (wiki/concepts/Interrupt Nesting.md)

timing_model.description: IntRace's S component encodes periodicity. Racebench guarantees none, so S is left unconstrained. Assuming a timing model the subject does not guarantee is an unsound filter (Pipeline Design, stage 2, 'Timing').

externals.description: Functions with no body in the module — library calls, vendor blobs, inline assembly. LLift's 'inherent knowledge boundary'.

default.description: The sound default: an unmodelled external may read and write any shared location reachable from its arguments, and any global. 'none' is unsound and is only for experiments — the manifest records it so results using it are identifiable.

models.description: Hand-modelled externals, the same closed-set argument that settled Specification Inference. Which functions were modelled and which were left opaque belongs in the assumption list.

alias.description: MUST be may-alias. A must-alias shortcut here silently deletes candidates (Pipeline Design, stage 1.2).

indirect_calls.description: An indirect call whose targets cannot be resolved is treated as potentially calling every address-taken function with a matching signature. 'points-to-only' trusts SVF's target set and is unsound when it resolves to nothing.

candidate_classes.description: Pairs and triples are derived separately from ONE access set. Do not derive triples by joining confirmed pairs (wiki/concepts/Pair-Triple Unification.md).

allow_same_statement_a1_a2.description: Allow A1 == A2 when the statement lies in a loop that may iterate more than once. Turning this off loses a substantial share of the ground truth (svp_simple_029_001).

on_timeout.description: A timeout is never SAT and never a drop. Fixed by decree (Roadmap W6–W7).

ground_truth.description: Optional. Points the evaluation harness at annotated ground truth for this subject (W2).
